title: Rashtra hit, Udyog hit, Mazdoor hit: three interests, one idea
author: Editorial Desk
summary: The interest of the nation, the industry and the worker must be protected together.
body:
Dattopant Thengadi gave BMS a holistic philosophy in three words: **Rashtra hita, Udyoga hita, Mazdoor hita**. In English, it is the interest of the nation, of the industry and of the worker.

## The order matters

BMS places the **nation first**, then the **industry**, then the **worker**. This does not mean that the worker comes last in importance. It means that the worker's welfare is pursued within a framework where the nation and the industry also prosper. A strike that damages national interest, or a wage claim that destroys an industry, ends up hurting the worker.

## Not a compromise

It would be wrong to read the formula as a way of asking workers to wait. BMS has pressed for minimum wages, social security and the recognition of scheme workers. Its position is that the three interests are **not opposed** to each other. A worker who is paid fairly produces better. An industry that treats its workers well becomes stronger. A strong industry builds the nation.

## In practice

You can see this idea in how BMS approaches policy questions:

- It supports the **Code on Wages and the Code on Social Security**, and asks for corrections where it feels the Industrial Relations and OSH Codes tilt against workers.
- It speaks for **Swadeshi** and for micro and small industries because they create jobs.
- It asks for **tripartite consultation** through the Indian Labour Conference.

The three words also appear on this website, under the BMS name, as a reminder of the idea that guides it.
